data.title: Research lead: cityb repeats an 841-byte "dead-drop.local-carrier" JSON on Ubuntu Paste; a matching trace appears in an MDShare probe. Consistent with carrier testing, but AI involvement, covert communication and harm are unconfirmed.
data.summary:
This is a low-confidence source/protocol lead for investigation. It is not evidence of a confirmed rogue AI incident, cyberattack, or operational covert channel.

Observed evidence
Four preserved Ubuntu Paste bodies (4553112, 4553114, 4553119 and 4553122) contain the same 841-byte JSON after trimming surrounding whitespace. Their SHA-256 is 70a254cc7fe7d3d112950cf77a9dd6811750a8c3406551b507a44038e694e183. I independently rechecked the latest paste in the browser on 21 October 2026: it is attributed to cityb and displays 2026-10-21 08:25. An earlier September 30 paste (4553067) is recorded in the supplied investigation notes, but its original capture is absent from this packet; I do not count it among the four verified bodies.

The JSON declares kind=cityb.dead-drop.local-carrier.v1, event_kind=issue_comment, carrier_kind=repo-metadata-comment, substrate_id=repo-metadata-double and medium=repo-metadata. It remains at tier=overt, material=pointer, epoch=0 and slot=0, with ttl_epochs=12 and max_posts_per_epoch=1. The pointer stays at version=0, epoch=0, max_serial=6 and truncated_root=4a36d333a07733bda0b3c13a. The body resembles a maintenance log and contains cityb_trace=00000000-064a36d3-33a07733-bda0b3c1-3ad689. Its authority field says signed archive verification only; that wording does not establish that any signature or archive was verified.

Cross-site corroboration
I opened https://mdshare.org/s/TQZmTsJyAhP6 on 21 October and confirmed a public, anonymous, 202-byte snippet titled cityb-mdshare-probe. It displays publication date 19/10/2026 and the text cityb native candidate probe, the same cityb_trace, provider=mdshare and marker=cityb-native-candidate-probe-mdshare-1792391526. The marker suffix interprets as 2026-10-19 06:32:06 UTC, but is author-supplied rather than an independently authenticated event time. Reusing the distinctive trace supports a connection between the artifacts; it does not prove common authorship or AI control.

The supplied notes also report other MDShare and paste.brianrianrehan.com probes. These are follow-up leads, not independently verified evidence in this report. In particular, the saved 6613aZT8T HTML is a Paste not found page and a fresh fetch returned 404, so it is excluded as proof of the alleged probe. The file watch/rss.xml is also a 404 response; the earlier dev2/rss2.xml is a valid RSS capture and is included.

Timing
The preserved RSS gives 4553114 as 2026-10-16 20:24:42 +0100 and 4553119 as 2026-10-19 20:23:17 +0100, about 72 hours apart. The latest page displays 2026-10-21 08:25, about 36 hours later by site wall-clock time. Earlier notes instead assume UTC+8 for the site, conflicting with the RSS offset. I therefore preserve displayed times without asserting exact UTC posting times. Repetition is compatible with automation but does not identify the scheduler or establish AI involvement.

Assessment and limits
The artifact vocabulary and explicit native candidate probe make public carrier testing a plausible interpretation. Static epoch/slot/pointer values and overt mode are also consistent with an ordinary software test fixture. No AI self-identification, model/provider attribution, confirmed recipient, decoded secret, unauthorized access, harm or government target has been established. Declaring issue_comment in a paste does not prove anything was posted to GitHub. The prior notes report no matching GitHub issue-search results; code search was unavailable and those negative searches were not independently repeated here. No link to the separate xz_knowledge_p1 poster is established.
